svg.text: Testing principles
functional (unit, integration, system, regression) and nonfunctional
(performance, load, stress, recovery); small services are easier to test;
this chapter covers testing methods specific to event-driven systems
Unit tests
stateless: test the filter and the map separately, including boundaries
(type 4 and 5, <=3, >=6) and nulls; stateful: a mocked or temporary store
(addValueToAggregation sums per key); fail the test if boundaries change
Topology tests (Ex 20-1)
no broker needed: Spark (StreamingSuiteBase, spark-fast-tests,
ContinuousMemoryStream), Flink (MiniClusterWithClientResource), Kafka Streams
(TopologyTestDriver); control timestamps, partitions, out-of-order and invalid
events; example: pipe 'a' with 1 and 2, expect 3, and nothing extra in the output
Schema evolution tests (Ex 20-2 to 20-5)
register the User schema for a subject, then POST the candidate (without age)
to the registry's compatibility endpoint for the latest version; read
is_compatible with jq; deploy only if true (default BACKWARD allows deleting
fields and adding optional ones); other registries differ
Integration testing: emulate event-stream and request inputs; the goal can be a smoke test or hundreds of input and output combinations. Three variations: local (a
local replica of production), remote (staging, QA or production) and hybrid (for example a local container against remote stores and brokers). Questions: what is the
goal; must it restart from the beginning or restore from a snapshot; what data decides success; performance, load or scaling needs; how to lower the barrier so each
service does not need its own harness. More services in a test means more complexity and omitted cases.
